questions.prompt: The loop must not start the next turn until a listener has finished writing a file. Which announcement should it use?
options: serial, because it waits for each listener to finish before returning
Either; they behave the same for async listeners
questions.explanation: emit calls listeners and returns at once without waiting. serial awaits each listener, so when it returns every one has finished.

questions.prompt: With the emit in this lesson, the first of three listeners throws. What happens to the other two?
options: They still run, because each call is wrapped in its own try and catch
They are skipped because emit stops at the first error
The error is passed to them as an argument
questions.explanation: emit catches and logs each listener's error separately, so one failure cannot stop later listeners from running.

questions.prompt: Why does unloading stepCounter stop the printing without any change to the agent loop?
options: The loop checks which plugins are loaded before announcing
serial skips listeners older than one turn
Registering the listener was an effect, so its disposer removed it from the list
The loop has to be restarted after any plugin unloads
questions.explanation: on() is built on effect(), and its disposer filters the listener out. The loop keeps announcing; there is simply no one listening.
